title: Policy Resolver Runtime Adapter and Audit Forwarder for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Nair
description:
Problem: current auth middleware is scattered (API gateway, console, runtime) and evaluates policies with duplicated logic and inconsistent audit records. We need a single low-latency policy resolver that can run in the runtime path (in-proc or sidecar), plus an audit forwarder that guarantees tamper-evident, ordered audit events to downstream sinks.

Goal: build a Policy Resolver Runtime Adapter (PRRA) that: (1) evaluates RBAC v2 policies with attribute-driven predicates, (2) can be embedded as a WASM module or deployed as a lightweight sidecar, (3) exposes a small stable gRPC/HTTP interface used by API/runtime/console middleware, (4) returns explainable decisions and decision-deltas for observability, and (5) emits audit events to a guaranteed-forwarding Audit Forwarder which batches, signs, and ships events to Kafka and S3 with backpressure handling.

Scope: authorization evaluation for token/API requests, admin console actions, and runtime internal control-plane calls. Does NOT include UI for policy authoring (PM work), but includes decision metadata required by console rollouts (explainability, matched rules, policy version).

Key characteristics: sandboxed evaluation (WASM), policy language: CEL for predicates + JSON path for attributes, compact policy cache with TTL/invalidations, deny-by-default fallback, deterministic ordering of side-effects for audit integrity, and an audit forwarder that supports both synchronous ack (for high-security calls) and async bulk shipment (for cost-efficiency).
acceptance_criteria: A1: PRRA exposes a stable gRPC endpoint: Check(permission_request) -> {allow|deny, reasons[], policy_version, eval_latency_ms}.
A2: Embedded WASM path must evaluate a representative policy set (1000 rules) with p50 < 0.7ms and p95 < 5ms for in-proc use on a c5.4xlarge-equivalent CPU.
A3: Sidecar path must meet p50 < 2ms and p95 < 15ms including RPC overhead for colocated services.
A4: Audit Forwarder batches events and persists to Kafka with at-least-once delivery; audit lag < 30s for async mode under normal load.
A5: Decision explainability present in response and captured in audit event (matched rule ids, attributes used).
A6: Rollout via feature flag with canary traffic routing and automatic rollback if denial rate increases > 5x baseline.
A7: E2E tests for console, API gateway, and runtime paths exercising SSO/SAML-constructed group attributes and admin flag checks.
design_notes: We will compile CEL predicates to WASM for sandboxed, language-agnostic execution; fallback interpreter for older stacks.
Policy bundle format: gzipped JSON with metadata header (version, signed_by) and provenance to be verified by runtime during load.
Cache: two-layer cache: (1) compiled-policy cache keyed by bundle SHA, (2) decision cache keyed by hashed request attributes with TTL and explicit invalidation on policy rollout.
Audit integrity: events signed with a rotating HMAC key; forwarder writes to Kafka topic 'audit.events.v2' then copies raw payloads to S3 for long-term retention.
Failure modes: on forwarder overload, auth decisions still returned but audit is marked 'deferred' and retried; for high-sensitivity paths we allow synchronous write+ack before returning 200.
implementation_details: Core evaluator implemented in Rust with Wasmtime for embed, exposes gRPC + HTTP binary proto for speed.
Sidecar binary is the same artifact run as a process with a small shim to expose unix-socket and HTTP endpoints for local services.
Audit Forwarder uses librdkafka, buffers to local WAL (append-only file) for durability, and a background uploader to Kafka/S3; metrics exposed via Prometheus.
Policy ingestion pipeline: git-backed bundles -> CI signing -> policy-registry service -> runtime pulls via signed endpoints with ETag-based cache control.
Policy versioning: every load annotated with deployment-id, git-commit, and policy-compiler-version; returned in decision metadata.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary on infra and vault services (5% traffic) using sidecar path + feature flag. Phase 2: expand to non-critical API routes and console-read actions (25% traffic). Phase 3: enable on all control-plane calls and admin write operations with synchronous audit enabled. At each phase run a 48-hour monitoring window and automated rollback on prespecified thresholds (denial rate, latency regression, audit backlog).
security_considerations: WASM sandbox reduces code injection risk; still enforce strict attestation and limit system calls.
Rotate HMAC keys for audit signing; integrate with KMS and support HSM for enterprise customers.
Deny-by-default ensures policy gaps do not silently grant access.
Ensure SAML attribute-to-group mapping is canonicalized to prevent privilege escalation via malformed attributes.
risks: Policy eval hot path may add latency to critical requests—mitigated by caching and local embed path.
Audit pipeline backpressure could cause high-latency synchronous calls; mitigated by selective sync vs async modes.
Policy misconfiguration may cause mass denials—require policy dry-run mode and preflight checks before rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for CEL->WASM compilation and predicate equivalence.
Load test harness simulating 10k req/s with realistic attribute distributions and 1000-rule bundles.
Chaos tests that kill forwarder/uploaders to verify WAL and retry correctness.
Integration tests covering SSO/SAML group mapping, console admin operations, and end-to-end audit ingestion.
comments: 2025-01-30 | Miguel Santos: Spike complete. Prototype WASM evaluator + gRPC shim works. Observed p50=0.55ms for simple rule-set on dev machine. Next: add compiled policy caching and WAL-backed audit buffer.
2025-02-04 | Aisha Nair (PM): Confirmed acceptance criteria with SRE and Compliance. Compliance requested signed audit chain and retention policy parameterization (90/365 days configurable).
2025-02-10 | Emma Liu (Security): Raised concern about attribute canonicalization for SAML. Action: add normalizer in SSO pipeline and add tests for unicode/whitespace variants.
2025-02-14 | Miguel Santos: Implemented local WAL for audit forwarder and initial Kafka producer. Integration tests failing intermittently under sustained load; investigating backpressure handling.
next_steps: Complete compiled-policy cache with invalidation hooks (ENG-45234 will expose rollout webhooks).
Add SAML attribute normalizer module and end-to-end test for group mapping (blocker for console admin write paths).
Instrument detailed histograms for per-rule eval time to identify slow predicates and add opt-in JIT for hot predicates.
Schedule security review with Compliance and SRE after audit signing integration.
